{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Scope:** Playbook review of the Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement. Findings below are drawn solely from the verified review record.

---

## 1. Executive summary

This agreement reviews well from our side. Of the eighteen playbook rules tested, seventeen are compliant — either at or above our preferred position — and one records a deviation (limitation of liability). Notably, no walk-away trigger is present anywhere in the document.

The commercial architecture is materially favourable to us as the exploiting licensee. We hold an exclusive licence with affiliate, sublicence and subcontractor reach (§ 3.1, § 3.4), a unilateral termination-for-convenience right exercisable in whole or country-by-country / Product-by-Product with no early-termination fee (§ 12.2(a)(i)), an uncapped counterparty indemnity carved out of the liability limitation (§§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.5), free assignment to Affiliates and to an M&A successor without consent (§ 15.2), and New York governing law with domestic JAMS arbitration (§§ 15.5, 15.6). The agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-purchase or liquidated-damages obligation on us, and Commercialization forecasts are expressly non-binding.

The single deviation is the absence of any aggregate monetary cap in § 14.5, which is a mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages only. Direct-damages exposure is therefore unlimited for both parties and the clause fails the fallback on the "cap exists" term. Because that finding did not clear verification, we recommend re-verifying it against the execution text before issuing the redline.

A secondary workstream is diligence rather than negotiation: several material figures are redacted as `[***]` (convenience notice period, audit notice/frequency/look-back/underpayment threshold, arbitration seat, transition windows, the "Competing Product" definition, and part of § 10.1(a)). These do not change our current assessment but must be confirmed on the unredacted execution version.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.5, 14.6) | Counterparty indemnity covers negligence/willful misconduct, warranty breach and breach of obligations; uncapped via § 14.5 carve-out — better than the fallback super-cap. No standalone allegation-based IP indemnity and a knowledge-qualified non-infringement warranty are noted only. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Intellectual Property Rights (Art. X; §§ 3.1, 3.5, 6.2) | Inventorship-based ownership, no assignment of our IP; joint technology carries an unrestricted right to exploit and licence without accounting or consent, so the joint-ownership walk-away does not arise. § 10.1(a) partly redacted. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | General Provisions (§ 15.2; § 12.2(a)(ii)) | We may assign to Affiliates and to an M&A successor without consent; counterparty assignment requires our consent, with Acquiror-Family firewall conditions. No counterparty termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | License (Art. III; §§ 3.6, 7.1–7.3) | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation on us; all exclusivity runs in our favour. Co-Promotion Option and § 12.2(d) are not exclusive-dealing covenants. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§ 12.2(a)(i), 12.3(c); §§ 9.6, 15.6(f)) | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us. Late-payment interest is mutual and statutorily capped; punitive damages are barred in arbitration. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | License (§§ 3.1(a), 3.4, 12.2, 12.3) | Exclusive licence, not revocable at the counterparty's discretion; extends to Affiliates, sublicensees and subcontractors; becomes perpetual and royalty-free on expiration. Consent for sublicensing substantially all US rights noted only. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Term and Termination (§ 12.2(d); §§ 3.8, 13.3–13.4, 15.2) | No restrictive covenant binds us; "Field" is any and all uses. § 12.2(d) creates a termination right only, defeasible by our written election, with no post-term restraint. "Competing Product" definition is redacted. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§ 12.1, 12.2, 12.3(c)) | Unilateral convenience right for us, including partial termination; counterparty has cause-based rights only. Notice period redacted — confirm it is no longer than 90 days. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (§ 9.9) | Mutual, notice-based, frequency-capped, defined look-back, independent auditor subject to our acceptance, records-only (no systems access), auditor-pays default. Thresholds redacted. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (§§ 15.5, 15.6) | New York law with no conflicts reference; mutual JAMS domestic arbitration in English, with court routes for patent validity and interim relief. Arbitration seat is redacted — confirm it is New York or another accepted US location. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (Art. IX) | No MFN, matching or "no less favourable" obligation; economics are fixed figures. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Commercialization (§§ 7.3, 8.x) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; forecasts expressly non-binding; we retain sole control of ordering, pricing and distribution. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 13.3 Covenants by RevMed (and § 13.4) | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant anywhere in the agreement; the absence benefits us. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant (rule not implicated) | Term and Termination (§§ 12.1, 12.2(a)) | Single self-executing term keyed to expiry of payment obligations; no renewal term, notice window or renewal-linked uplift. Exit is unilateral at our discretion. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | Confidentiality; Publication (§ 11.6; §§ 12.3(b)–(e), 12.4) | Mutual return/destruction on written request with retention carve-outs; defined transition assistance and regulatory/clinical data transfer; our licences go perpetual on expiry. Post-termination windows redacted. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Research (§ 4.2(b); Art. XIII) | Substantive performance standard (GMP/GLP/GCP), extensive title, non-infringement and compliance warranties, with a JRDC cure process, step-in rights, indemnity and termination remedies. § 13.5 disclaimer expressly preserves Art. XIII, so no "AS IS" exposure. Warranties given as of the Execution Date, with a closing bring-down. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant (at fallback) | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.6) | Mutual insurance covenant including product liability, certificates on request, and one-way pre-cancellation notice to us; self-insurance permitted for us and insurance is not a cap on indemnity. Limits set by market practice rather than stated figures. |
| 18 | Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** (verification: fail — re-verify before issuing) | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.5) | § 14.5 waives indirect, consequential, incidental and punitive damages and lost profits, with carve-outs for §§ 14.1/14.2 indemnification and Art. X/XI breaches, but contains no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the agreement, so direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties and the fallback is not met. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

None. No finding in this review reached walk-away territory:

- **Indemnity** is present, mutual in structure and uncapped in our favour (§§ 14.1, 14.5).
- **IP** is not assigned away, and joint ownership carries an unrestricted right to exploit and licence without accounting or consent — the joint-ownership walk-away does not apply (§ 10.1(b)).
- **Audit** is records-only, with no remote or direct systems access (§ 9.9).
- **Warranty** is not disclaimed on an "AS IS" basis; § 13.5 preserves Article XIII in full.
- **Data return** is on request with retention carve-outs, not immediate deletion, and our licences become perpetual on expiry (§§ 11.6, 12.3(b)).
- **Forum** is domestic US arbitration under JAMS, not foreign arbitration or a foreign venue (§ 15.6(a)).

Two redactions are the only items capable of changing that conclusion, and both are watch-items rather than current issues: the arbitration **seat** in § 15.6(a) (a seat outside the accepted US list would change our governing-law/venue assessment) and the definition of **"Competing Product"** (whose breadth we cannot presently verify).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify the § 14.5 finding.** This is our only deviation and it did not clear verification. Before any redline goes out, confirm against the execution text that no aggregate liability cap appears elsewhere in the agreement or in the side Letter or Profit/Loss Share Agreement.
2. **If confirmed, propose the § 14.5 repair.** Keep the existing waiver and carve-out sentence intact; extend the carve-outs to data protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud as a defined set of "Excluded Claims"; and add one sentence imposing a **mutual** cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, confirming that our payment obligations are not damages. Note that the current uncapped position cuts both ways, so we should take a commercial view on whether we prefer symmetry or the status quo before tabling this.
3. **Clear the redactions on the unredacted execution version.** Specifically: the § 12.2(a)(i) convenience notice period (confirm no longer than 90 days); the § 9.9 audit notice period, frequency, look-back and underpayment percentage (preferred 30 days / once per 12 months / 5%; fallback 15 days / 10%); the § 15.6(a) arbitration seat (confirm New York or another accepted US location); the § 12.3(c)(vi) transition time periods; the "Competing Product" definition; and the redacted portion of § 10.1(a) on inventorship allocation.
4. **Confirm commercially, not legally.** The § 12.3(c)(vi) effort and duration limits on transition assistance and the § 14.6 insurance limits (set by market practice rather than stated figures) are business calls for the deal team, not playbook breaches.
5. **No other redlines.** The remaining sixteen compliant findings require no amendment, and several provisions run in our favour and should not be disturbed — in particular our self-insurance right and the non-capping of indemnity in § 14.6, the post-termination royalties payable to us under § 12.3(c)(ii)(C), and the absence of any non-solicit, MFN or minimum-commitment obligation.

*This memo relies solely on the findings supplied and does not extend to provisions outside the rules tested.*"}
